sources.title: Hernán and Robins, Causal Inference: What If, updated 2026 author-hosted edition
sources.locator: Chapter 2, printed pp. 13–25, Technical Points 2.2–2.3; Chapter 3, printed pp. 27–45, especially exchangeability, positivity, consistency, identifiability and Technical Point 3.1.

contents.name: Technical Point 2.2, formal definition of inverse-probability weights
Technical Point 2.3, equivalence of standardization and IP weighting and the displayed derivations
contents.reason: The source derivations were independently reconstructed with conditional-expectation classes and a local integrable-factorization lemma; no source proof is substituted for the local arguments.

contents.name: Technical Point 2.3, exchangeability and consistency routes from the standardized and weighted means to the potential-outcome mean
contents.reason: The source route was used as an independent check; the local proof supplies integrability for unbounded outcomes and propensities that are positive but not bounded away from zero.

contents.name: Chapter 3, exchangeability, positivity and consistency conditions and their interpretation
contents.reason: The local theorem states these as assumptions on a specified causal model and proves only the resulting population identity; it does not claim that observational data verify them.

contents.name: Technical Point 3.1, loss of identification when treatment positivity fails
contents.reason: The example independently constructs two full-data laws with the same observed law and different target means, retaining its own complete finite verification.

contents.name: Technical Point 2.3, continuous-treatment density weights and their separate support issues
contents.reason: The controlling SME-21 plan limits the proved formulas to discrete or atomic treatment and requires a separately declared density or intervention functional for continuous treatment.

sources.title: The Mathematics of Indirect Treatment Comparisons, Chapters 9–10
sources.locator: Chapter 9, §§9.3–9.5 and Theorem 9.3; Chapter 10, §§10.1–10.5, especially Lemma 10.1 and Theorems 10.3–10.4 with their complete proofs.

contents.name: Chapter 9, Theorem 9.3 adjustment formula and standardization proof
contents.reason: This is an independent derivation; its binary-treatment, square-integrability and uniform-overlap hypotheses are stronger than the local fixed-atom theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 10, Lemma 10.1 regression identity and Theorem 10.3 inverse-probability weighting proof
contents.reason: This supplies a second complete proof route; the local argument retains merely almost-sure positivity and proves weighted integrability from integrable potential outcomes.

contents.name: Chapter 10, Theorem 10.4 standardization proof
contents.reason: This independently checks the conditional-regression and tower-property steps without importing its stronger standing assumptions.
